decisions.reason: Allowing the power-connector pins to be reordered does not necessarily change connector placement, orientation, accessibility, or mounting-hole clearance.
The power-connector pin-order policy does not alter the four-layer PCB stack.
Optimizing pin order for layout does not necessarily change the board dimensions, installation orientation, USB-C placement, aspect ratio, or mounting arrangement.
The source decision concerns the power connector's pin order and does not change I2C cable length, bus speed, pull-up resistance, or pull-up location.
The charge-status display method and GPIO remain unchanged by the power-connector pin reordering.
The source decision does not change the selected USB-C connector, its data support, sourceability, or substitution requirements.
The addressable-LED family and GPIO are unaffected by reordering the separate interboard power-connector pins.
The battery connector is a separate interface, and the source does not change its family, pitch, pin count, pin functions, or part number.
Reordering the 5V and 3.3V positions on an interboard connector does not change the boost converter's enable control, default state, or powered loads.
The source decision does not change the battery NTC terminal, its J_BAT connection, or thermal-protection behavior.
The battery protection controller and voltage cutoffs remain valid regardless of the interboard power-connector pin order.
The source concerns the separate power connector and does not modify the native USB D+ and D- interface.
